newsitem.title: USA: Calif. regulators amend SBC, PacTel merger proposals.
newsitem.headline: Calif. regulators amend SBC, PacTel merger proposals.

text.p: Several California regulators Monday proposed approving SBC Communications Inc.'s $17 billion merger with Pacific Telesis Group with sharply reduced customer refunds.
The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is the only regulatory body whose approval of the merger is still needed.

Two of the five CPUC commissioners, Josiah Neeper and Richard Bilas, proposed that Pacific Telesis unit Pacific Bell refund $248 million to customers over five years as a condition for the CPUC approving the deal.
Commission president Gregory Conlon issued a separate proposal, suggesting that Pacific Bell refund $315.67 million to ratepayers over eight years.
Both proposed refunds were sharply lower than the $590.5 million refund over five years proposed last month by two administrative law judges who make recommendations to the CPUC.

Pacific Telesis and SBC said that, with inflation, Pacific Bell would have to refund $750 million under the judges' proposal and said that could jeopardize the merger if adopted. The companies had urged the five commissioners to reject the judges' proposal and approve the merger without conditions.
The companies and other interested parties have 10 days to comment on the proposals issued Monday.

The panel could vote on all three proposals at a meeting scheduled for March 31 or it could narrow down the proposals before voting, CPUC sources said. A majority of three commissioners is needed for a proposal to be approved.
The various refund proposals are based on widely differing calculations of the cost savings that will accrue to the two companies as a result of the planned merger.
Representatives of the companies, consumer groups and experts presented widely different estimates of cost savings to the commission, ranging from $366 million to $3.7 billion.
California law requires the commission to share projected economic benefits of a merger between shareholders and ratepayers, with ratepayers receiving not less than half of the benefits.

The administrative law judges forecast the total economic benefits of the merger at $1.18 billion. Neeper and Bilas estimated them at $495 million. Conlon estimated the benefits at $690.38 million less the funds Pacific Bell has promised to contribute to a program to improve telecommunications access for underserved communities.

SBC Communications and Pacific Telesis Group said Neeper and Bilas's proposal was "a step in the right direction" but fell short "of what the record and CPUC precedent says should be done." By the companies' calculation, taking account of inflation, the proposal calls for more than $330 million in payments to California customers and other conditions.

Dick Odgers, Pacific Telesis general counsel, said the new proposal "fails to recognize the full extent of benefits this merger will bring to California." While it was "a step in the right direction", he said he did not believe that the payment to customers was warranted.
Pacific Telesis spokesman Lou Saviano said he had no immediate comment on Conlon's proposal because the company had not yet seen it.
